name: Kubl
tagline: Orri Erling's lightweight Finnish SQL engine from the 1990s that became the core of OpenLink Virtuoso.
description: Kubl was a compact, high-performance relational (later object-relational) database written by Orri Erling in Finland, with development starting in 1994 and partly funded by the Infosto Group for its online classified-ads services. A free trial was published in November 1996, and it was marketed as a fast, lightweight engine for embedded use with an emphasis on transaction-per-second benchmarks. In 1998 OpenLink Software acquired Kubl and hired Erling, and Kubl's engine became the heart of OpenLink Virtuoso, which still ships today as a SQL and RDF/SPARQL server. Kubl itself has not been sold since; anyone interested should look at Virtuoso.
statusNote: Acquired by OpenLink Software in 1998 and folded into OpenLink Virtuoso, which remains the maintained successor.

pricing.notes: A free trial was offered from 1996; product withdrawn after the 1998 acquisition.

strengths: Lean, fast SQL engine built for high transaction rates
Its design survives in OpenLink Virtuoso's relational core
Embeddable footprint unusual for 1990s SQL databases
weaknesses: Discontinued since 1998; no binaries or documentation in circulation
Known today only through Virtuoso's history
useCases: History of Virtuoso and of Finnish database engineering
Background when tracing Virtuoso's relational engine design
